questions.q: What does an Administrator do, per this lesson, that's different from a Technical Architect's job?
options: Configures and maintains the platform within established patterns, rather than deciding what those patterns are
Decides whether the instance should be single-instance or multi-instance
Sets the integration pattern every future integration must follow
Owns the long-term consequences of a platform-wide design decision
questions.explain: Admins work within rules someone else set — users, groups, ACLs, notifications, update sets — not the rules themselves.

questions.q: What is the real boundary between an admin/developer decision and an architect decision?
options: Architect decisions always involve harder code
Consequence and reversibility — how expensive or impossible the decision is to undo once others build on it
Architect decisions are always made by the most senior person in the room
There is no real boundary; the titles are interchangeable
questions.explain: It's not about difficulty — a developer can write harder code. It's about how costly the decision is to reverse once teams depend on it.

questions.q: A developer wants to use IntegrationHub for one integration to a payroll vendor, local to that integration. What kind of decision is this, per the lesson's own example?
options: An architect decision regardless of scope
An admin decision, since it involves configuration
A developer decision, because it's local to that one integration
Not a real decision at all
questions.explain: The lesson frames this exact example: it becomes an architect decision only if it sets the pattern every future integration on the platform must follow.

questions.q: Besides producing designs, what is one concrete responsibility this lesson assigns to a Technical Architect?
options: Leading design review of work admins and developers produce, to catch platform-wide impact they can't see locally
Writing every scoped application's business rules personally
Approving every notification an admin configures
Avoiding any contact with admins or developers on a project
questions.explain: Design review, setting standards, mentoring, and long-term accountability are the four responsibilities the lesson names beyond design work itself.

questions.q: Why does this lesson say an architect carries accountability "over time"?
options: Because architects are paid more than admins or developers
Because if a platform decision causes real pain years later, the architect who made that call owns that outcome long after the original project closed
Because architects must personally fix every bug a developer introduces
Because accountability only applies during the exact week a decision is made
questions.explain: Unlike a reversible admin or dev change, an architectural decision's consequences can surface years later — and the architect who made it still owns them.
